provenance.l: collectSPACE: Athena's orbit was lowered to about 10 km near the site; the main engine relit about 15 minutes before touchdown and at about 2 km the lander pitched to mostly upright. Spaceflight Now: the powered descent started at about 4,000 mph (1.8 km/s). The model brakes from 10 km and 1,800 m/s, pitches over at 2.5 km and lands 12.6 minutes later (Wikipedia's 17:27 UTC start conflicts with the 15 minutes)
NASA: the planned terminal descent slowed to about 3 m/s at 30 m and 1 m/s from 10 m, on inertial data alone; touchdown about 17:30 UTC on 6 Mar 2025

Intuitive Machines (LROC 1408 caption): Athena hit the surface faster than intended and came to rest on its side in a 20 m crater at 84.7906 S, 29.1957 E. The laser altimeter's readings were noisy all the way down. A report of 10 to 13 m/s could not be opened: the model touches down at 10 m/s, and the speed is unverified
Nova-C VR900 engine: 3,100 N per Wikipedia (a 4,000 N figure also circulates). IM-2 launched at 2,120 kg (Wikipedia); the mass at the start of the descent is not published: estimates
